item.title: UAE: Over 3,600 people convert to Islam in Dubai in first half of 2025
item.description: Over 3,600 people embraced Islam in Dubai during the first half of 2025 through the Mohammed bin Rashid Centre for Islamic Culture. The Centre also enrolled 1,300+ students and conducted educational initiatives, including immersive learning via the Sustainable Knowledge Room. Operating under IACAD, the Centre promotes religious awareness, intercultural dialogue, and structured Islamic education across Dubai.

item.title: “We’re proud of each other”: Taylor Swift shared the heartfelt reason for going public with Travis Kelce after years of keeping her relationships private
item.description: Taylor Swift openly embraced her relationship with Travis Kelce, contrasting sharply with her past privacy, particularly with Joe Alwyn. Swift explained to TIME that they proudly support each other, dismissing the need to hide their romance. Since 2023, they've been publicly affectionate, attending events and date nights, fueling engagement speculations.

item.title: UAE: Students must confirm university admissions and scholarships offers by August 11
item.description: The UAE Ministry of Higher Education has set August 11, 2025, as the final deadline for students to confirm university admissions and scholarships for the 2025–2026 academic year. Students must complete all procedures on time to avoid delays. Additionally, a new unified academic calendar for universities has been published to standardize term dates and holidays.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: SpaceX splashdown: ISS astronauts return after 5 months; Nasa’s first Pacific landing in 50 years
item.description: Four astronauts, including NASA's Anne McClain and Nichole Ayers, safely returned to Earth after a five-month mission on the ISS. Their SpaceX capsule splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off Southern California, marking SpaceX's first Pacific splashdown in 50 years. The mission replaced astronauts stranded due to Boeing's Starliner malfunctions.

item.title: Russia welcomes Armenia-Azerbaijan peace deal; hopes for stability in Caucasus
item.description: Russia has welcomed the draft peace agreement between Armenia and Azerbaijan, expressing hope for regional stability. Brokered in Washington with US mediation, the deal aims to end decades of hostility and establishes the 'Trump Route' transit corridor. This corridor will enhance Azerbaijan's access to European markets and signifies a shift in geopolitical influence towards the U.S. in the South Caucasus.

item.title: 'Over 200 arrested': London police crackdown on supporters of a pro-Palestinian group; protesters call it free speech violation
item.description: London police have arrested approximately 365 individuals after demonstrators openly defied a new law banning public support for 'Palestine Action,' a pro-Palestinian group. The arrests occurred during heightened demonstrations in London, including pro-Palestinian marches and rallies calling for the release of Israeli hostages. Protesters argue the legislation unfairly restricts freedom of expression, challenging the ban in court.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: What is Captagon? Saudi customs seize over 400,000 pills hidden in sheep wool at Haditha border
item.description: Saudi Arabia’s Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority (ZATCA) seized 406,400 Captagon pills hidden in sheep wool at the Haditha border. This bust follows recent major drug interceptions at Jeddah port and Saudi airports. Using advanced screening technologies, ZATCA continues to combat sophisticated smuggling tactics while cooperating regionally to curb the illegal Captagon trade threatening public health and security.

item.title: Armenia-Azerbaijan deal: Khamenei aide says Iran will oppose peace corridor near its border
item.description: Iran vehemently opposes the US-brokered peace agreement between Armenia and Azerbaijan, specifically the creation of the 'Trump Route' transit corridor. Tehran views the corridor as a threat to regional stability, fearing it will sever Iran's connection to Armenia and allow foreign presence along its border. Iran has warned of potential intervention and has conducted military drills to demonstrate its resolve.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Who was Patrick Joseph White? Suspect in CDC shooting who killed an officer and was later found dead; probe under way
item.description: A shooting at the CDC headquarters in Atlanta resulted in the deaths of both the gunman, Patrick Joseph White, and DeKalb County Police Officer David Rose. White opened fire outside the CDC campus, striking multiple buildings before being found dead inside. The motive remains unknown, and the incident prompted a large-scale investigation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Earthquake strikes Russia: 6.1 magnitude tremor jolts Kurli Islands; comes days after 8.8 Kamchatka quake
item.description: A 6.1 magnitude earthquake hit the Kuril Islands on Saturday. The National Center for Seismology reported the event. The quake occurred at a depth of 10 km. Its epicenter was at latitude 49.94°N and longitude 162.70°E. This follows an 8.8 magnitude earthquake off Russia’s Kamchatka Peninsula. A 5.1 magnitude tremor also occurred near Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky recently.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Poor judgment and...': Kash Patel's letter firing FBI agent Walter Giardina who lost wife last month goes viral
item.description: FBI Director Kash Patel fired agent Walter B. Giardina, who recently lost his wife to cancer and prosecuted Peter Navarro, accusing him of political weaponization. The dismissal letter went viral, sparking debate, with some criticizing Patel's timing and others supporting the decision, citing Giardina's alleged misconduct. Many said that the fact that Giardina leaked the letter showed his integrity.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Hezbollah military facility explosion: 5 soldiers killed while clearing munitions; Lebanese PM pays tributes
item.description: Five Lebanese soldiers tragically died in an explosion at a Hezbollah military facility near Majdal Zoun, Tyre district, while clearing munitions left over from the recent conflict with Israel. The facility was being dismantled by the Lebanese army under a November truce agreement.
